provenance.note: Two spectra and a crossfade between them, which is the linear interpolation a wavetable synthesiser actually computes.

notes.hollow: The first frame: odd harmonics at 1/n with the third and fifth pulled down, which is a closed pipe and reads dark and woody.
notes.humpAt: The second: every harmonic at 1/sqrt(n) with a hump five partials up, which is what makes a spectrum read as a mouth rather than as a filter.
notes.layers: `[octave, level, pan]`. The morph is between two *waves*, so the two oscillators of a pair may not be detuned — that would be a flanger — and the width is a second pair an octave up instead.
